title: Prediction Markets: Last Week Tonight with John Oliver (HBO)
summary: A comedy news segment on prediction markets argues most users lose, insiders and manipulators win, the hedging framing dodges gambling law, and regulators are not enforcing existing limits.

assertions.quote: researchers have found that most users of Kalshi and Polymarket lose money.

verdicts.note: On-chain analyses show a large majority of accounts are net losers with profits concentrated in a few hundred wallets, matching sportsbook and retail-trading patterns.

assertions.quote: prediction markets are not only able to operate in states where gambling isn't legal, but also get around state taxes and minimum age requirements

verdicts.note: Federal commodity-exchange registration is the stated basis for operating nationally; multiple states are suing on exactly this point.

assertions.quote: roughly consistent with those of professional forecasters when it came to the economy and Federal Reserve policy, but they've also had some big misses

verdicts.note: Studies find calibration comparable to experts on liquid macro markets, with thin markets and low-volume events showing large errors.

assertions.quote: for a lot of these bets, it is incredibly easy for individuals to manipulate the outcomes.
There have also been multiple instances of people seeming to use inside information to game these markets.
around 90 percent of trading volume on Kalshi is on sports.

verdicts.note: Platform volume data show sports contracts dominate; the risk-hedging use case is a small share.

assertions.quote: the wisdom of crowds in the form of people putting actual money behind their opinions can produce useful forecasts

verdicts.note: Academic election markets have matched or beaten polls on average, but the advantage is modest and disappears in thin or manipulable markets.
Election markets have matched or modestly beaten polls on average, but the edge is small and fails in thin or manipulable markets.

assertions.quote: Kalshi told us that they paid him for that post.

verdicts.note: The segment confirmed one paid post; the broader pattern matches documented undisclosed promotion in sports betting and crypto.

assertions.quote: But it is clearly not doing that, and it doesn't even seem to be trying.

verdicts.note: Such contracts are live on major platforms despite statutory authority to prohibit them; the regulator has instead sued states that tried to intervene.
